questions.question: Explain what a realistic budget is and the three things a tender board reads it for, list the standard sections of a construction budget, and explain how the model's dimensions are scaled to budget the real headgear.
questions.expected_answer: A realistic budget is a reasoned, itemised estimate whose quantities are taken from the drawings and parts list and whose rates come from current market sources, so that every number can be checked. The board reads it for completeness, whether every part of the work is included; realism, whether quantities match the drawing and rates match current prices; and honesty, whether the working and sources are shown, treating an unusually low bid as a warning of omissions. The sections are materials with quantity, unit, rate and amount; labour by trade and time; plant and equipment hired by the day; design and professional fees, often a percentage; contingency of about 10 to 15 percent; value-added tax at 15 percent; and a summary with the date and basis of the rates and any exclusions. The real headgear is budgeted by multiplying the working drawing's model dimensions by the model-to-real factor, 1 to 100 for a 600 millimetre model of a 60 metre headgear, and scaling the parts list quantities accordingly, while the model itself is budgeted in rand on the same format as a check against its cost constraint.

questions.question: Describe how structural steel, foundations and specialist components are quantified and priced for a real headgear, and state what every budget line must show.
questions.expected_answer: Structural steel is quantified by taking the length of each section from the parts list, converting to mass with the section's kilograms per metre from a steel table and summing to tonnes, with the working shown, for example four legs of 62 metres at about 100 kilograms per metre giving 24.8 tonnes, plus bracing, beams and back-leg and an allowance of about 10 percent for connections; it is priced per tonne supplied, fabricated and erected at a rate quoted with source and date. Foundations are reinforced concrete bases under each leg and the back-leg, measured in cubic metres of concrete and tonnes of reinforcing with rates per unit. Specialist components are priced as units: two sheave wheel assemblies, winding rope per metre, and the winder with motor, gearbox, drum and brakes, which may be a separate contract and must be stated as included or excluded, plus platforms, stairs, guards, lighting, lightning protection, paint, shaft collar steel and guides. Every line shows item, quantity, unit, rate and amount, with the source of the quantity and of the rate, and lines whose rate cannot be found are estimated and marked as estimates rather than omitted.

questions.question: Explain how labour, plant, professional fees and the commonly forgotten items are costed, and how contingency and tax are added and the summary presented.
questions.expected_answer: Labour is costed by trade and time: the number of people of each trade, including erectors and riggers, boilermakers and welders, crane operators, concrete workers, electricians, mechanical fitters, surveyors, a safety officer, a supervisor and a project manager, multiplied by hours or days from the construction programme and by sourced rates, for example twelve people for thirty days at eight hours giving 2 880 hours. Plant is hired by the day, including a large mobile crane, scaffolding or access platforms, welding sets, generators and transport. Professional fees for design and supervision are typically 8 to 12 percent of construction cost. Often forgotten items are insurance, site establishment, environmental and safety measures such as dust and water management and waste disposal, and testing and commissioning. Contingency of 10 to 15 percent of the subtotal is stated as a percentage and an amount with its purpose, value-added tax of 15 percent is added, and the summary lists each section total, contingency, tax and grand total with the date of rates, sources, exclusions and assumptions, with the model budget presented on the same format in rand.
